title_as_printed: TABLE I. Solubility of methane (mol CH4/mol H2O x 10^3) in water and aqueous solutions
property_description: mole ratio of dissolved CH4 to water, n_CH4/n_H2O (mol CH4 per mol H2O), printed x10^3 in column alpha. Not a mole fraction. In the salt solutions the denominator is stated as mol H2O (water only; salt moles not included); x_CH4 (salt-free basis) = r/(1+r); molality of CH4 per kg water = r/0.0180153.
pressure_note: P column has no unit in the table; text and figures use atmospheres ('pressures up to 200 atm', manometer accuracy 0.02/0.1/1 atm, figure axes 'P Atm'). Synthetic pressure-decline method; whether P is total or CH4 partial pressure is not stated. For 100-150 C an estimated correction for water in the gas phase was applied to the amount of undissolved gas (text p. 804).

T.note: printed only on the first row of each temperature sub-block (degree sign stripped); blocks with no printed t get T.constant 25 from group_rows

composition.other_species: LiCl, NaBr, NaJ (= NaI) at 2.7 n; non-electrolytes cane sugar, glucose (1 and 2 gr. m. per L) and formaldehyde (2 gr. m. per L) as gram-molecules per litre (molarity). 'n' (italic) = normal, written '2,7 N' in the text.

skip_rows.reason: block label rows (solute and concentration); printed beside the first data row, written as own label rows (v2.1 rule 10)

conversion_needs: alpha x 1e-3 = mol CH4 per mol H2O; convert to mole fraction (salt-free: r/(1+r); with salt the builder must add the salt moles) or to CH4 molality per kg water (r/0.0180153).
Normality to molality needs solution density (not given). CaCl2 2.7 n = 1.35 mol/L CaCl2; the 1-1 salts 2.7 n = 2.7 mol/L.
Non-electrolyte solutions in gram-molecules per litre (molarity).
Pressure atm (unit from text, not table) to MPa x 0.101325.
notes: Table I is printed as four side-by-side column groups (t | P | alpha). Stacked in printed order: column 1 (NaCl series at 25 C), column 2 (LiCl, KCl, CaCl2, NaBr, NaJ at 2.7 n, then the non-electrolyte solutions, all 25 C), column 3 (NaCl 2.5 n at 50-125 C), column 4 (NaCl 2.5 n at 150 C, then NaCl 5.4 n at 50-150 C). The H2O blocks (column 1 at 25 C, 9 rows; column 3 at 50, 75, 100, 125, 150 C, 30 rows) are NOT written: water rows already in GasBrineBench (MICHELS(1936)). Only the H2O and LiCl block labels print 25 deg; the other 25 C blocks in columns 1 and 2 carry no temperature and are set to 25 C by column layout. NaCl 2.5 n at 50-125 C (column 3) and at 150 C (column 4) belong to the same 2.5 n temperature series; the label 'NaCl 2.5 n' is printed again at the head of column 4 and written as its own label row. The 25 C NaCl 2.5 n block (column 1) is a separate measurement series. 2026-10-11 coordinator: property set to solubility_mole_ratio (alpha x 1e-3 = mol CH4 per mol H2O, converted exactly to molality); NaCl normality converted with density_rule nacl_25C_1atm (flag density-assumed; the paper does not state at which temperature the normality is defined, presumably room temperature). Other salts and the non-electrolytes stay held.
